title: Flight in Nature and Technology
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Flight in Nature and Technology Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe how animals and seeds fly or glide; explain how people have used ideas from nature in flying devices; assess the social and environmental impacts of aviation and drones. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand D: Structures and Mechanisms – Flight)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on how birds, seeds and gliders fly, airplanes, drones, bush planes and the effects of air travel. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Birds, maple keys and dandelion seeds use the same forces as airplanes.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things and machines use the same four forces to fly.

  • Birds flap for thrust and have light, hollow bones; maple keys spin; dandelion seeds use parachutes.
  • People copied nature (biomimicry) to design wings, gliders and drones.
  • Air travel connects remote communities but adds pollution and noise.
Example

How does a maple key fall slowly?

it spins like a rotor

Answer: spinning makes lift

Example

Why do Canada geese fly in a V?

each bird rides on air from the one ahead

Answer: to save energy

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all birds can fly.
  • Thinking gliders have engines.
  • Thinking air travel has no effect on the environment.

faq.a: They reach communities in the north without roads, landing on lakes with floats in summer and skis in winter.

items.q: How do Canada geese save energy on long flights?
c: They fly in a V formation so each bird gets lift from the bird ahead.
items.e: The V shape reduces drag.

items.q: What is the job of a propeller?
c: to push air back and give thrust
items.e: Propeller blades are spinning airfoils.

items.q: Why do airplanes de-ice their wings in an Ontario winter?
c: Ice changes the wing shape and reduces lift.
items.e: A clean wing makes proper lift.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight grows when more passengers and bags are loaded?
items.e: That force is weight (gravity).

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight pushes the plane forward, made by the engines or propeller?

items.q: Why are airports often far from homes?
c: Airplanes are loud, and noise affects people nearby.
items.e: Noise is a social impact.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight pulls the plane down toward Earth?
items.e: That force is weight (gravity).

items.q: What is one way airplanes are designed to be safer?
c: They have backup systems and are tested in wind tunnels.
They do not check the weather.
items.e: Engineers test many times.
